chunks: Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I said to him: In how many (days) should I recite the Qur'an? He said: Recite it in fifths, recite it in sevenths. As for me, I have a codex divided into fourteen parts.
ai.seo_question: How should one divide the Qur'an for recitation according to the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the flexibility in the method of completing the Qur'an (Khatm), where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) permits divisions into fifths or sevenths while noting his own preference for a fourteen-part division. This reflects the scholarly tradition that emphasizes ease and accessibility in worship, allowing individuals to adapt recitation schedules to their capacity. The mention of a specific 'Mushaf' (codex) underscores the historical context of Qur'anic compilation and the practical application of these divisions in daily devotion.
